slides.headline: Lore beat slop
slides.aside: the word of the year is lore
slides.body: Sprout Social named “lore” its 2026 social media word of the year: over 10 million mentions, against 8.8 million for “slop”.
slides.take: As the cost of making anything goes to zero, what stands out is telling unique stories in ways that connect. It's not new. “Tell me a story” is the first thing kids ask for at bedtime. The winners will come from it.

slides.headline: A meme waited three years
slides.body: Since 2023, a singing polar bear has been reminding people that November 2026 is coming. A version from late August passed 980,000 views in two weeks. Now it's here.
slides.take: Everything is instant and disposable. Making something to be experienced at a later date takes discipline and foresight. That's how you cut through the noise.

slides.headline: Fans paying to watch fans
slides.body: BTS sold 252,000 tickets across three nights in São Paulo, and the cinema livestream made $3M in the US. Their first Brazil fan meeting, in 2014, held 1,500.
slides.take: Fans want to be connected to other fans. An event about the event. Artists who can build these moments, for films or concerts, will stand out. I'd love to see it at industry conferences too.

slides.headline: An NBA team will dress as a fake city

media.label: Miami Heat x Cactus Jack x Nike · SI

slides.body: On 18 Nov, the night before GTA VI launches, the Miami Heat wear “Vice City” jerseys with the GTA VI logo, sold at the arena that day.
slides.take: Brilliant. It shows GTA's cultural impact and the licensing opportunity around it. I'd love to see more IP crossovers in 2027, even local teams, to cross-pollinate fan bases.

slides.headline: One date stamp, and fans wrote the plot
slides.body: Bethesda's first Elder Scrolls 6 teaser in eight years shows no gameplay. Just a buried scroll, runes and an in-world date five years after Skyrim. Fans already have time-travel theories.

slides.headline: A band guarding its canon
slides.body: The masked band broke their silence to disown a former associate's project: “What is ours is here, and here alone.” When the mystery is the product, who gets to add to the story?

slides.headline: Harry Styles played his own origin story
slides.body: Closing 30 nights at Madison Square Garden, he dressed as his 2010 X Factor audition self, then as Pizza Rat on Halloween.
slides.take: People don't just love artists for their music. They love their stories, who they are, what they have to say. Once fans are devoted, they want to know everything.

slides.headline: Worlds you can play
slides.body: Genie 4 makes playable, real-time worlds you steer with text, with live sound and dialogue. Trusted testers only for now.
slides.take: Anybody can make anything doesn't mean great gaming survives. People play because the experience is rich. Outside of novelty, I don't think it lasts. For aspiring game makers, it makes a lot of sense.

slides.headline: Characters that stay the same
slides.body: Kling's new model holds a character steady across a 30-second scene, the hurdle that kept these tools from making recurring characters.
slides.take: Character consistency is the last hurdle. As Ed Catmull said, it's just another problem, and once it's solved, that's a good thing. Anyone who's used these tools knows the discipline it takes to make something that isn't slop.

slides.headline: A voice sold on its pauses
slides.body: Block's Dessa talks and listens at the same time, laughs and pauses, and runs on a laptop. Jack Dorsey's pitch: “full of emotion, nuance, pauses.” Not public yet.

slides.headline: Fanta built its own monsters
slides.body: After years of licensing Chucky and Freddy Fazbear, Fanta made four original monsters with GRAiL, an AI studio, in what it calls a “human-led” process. Live in 50 markets.

slides.headline: Steal the animated story short
slides.body: Its proof is a 67-second short about the 1831 Broughton bridge. Any history story, no filming, no archival footage.
slides.take: I don't buy “anyone can make anything.” Ruthless editing and the discipline to tell one idea coherently will become extremely valuable.
